svg.title: A fission chain reaction
svg.desc: A neutron strikes a uranium-235 nucleus, which splits into two fission fragments and three neutrons. Two of those neutrons strike other uranium-235 nuclei, which split in turn, and so on: each generation doubles the number of fissions, so the reaction sustains itself. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: The effective multiplication factor determines a chain reaction’s trend
Expected populations obey N(g) = N0 k^g; dots advance in discrete generations. Leakage and capture
are included in k. This mean model omits fluctuations, delayed neutrons and feedback.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
